faq.q: My AC isn't blowing cold air. What should I check first?
faq.a: Make sure the thermostat is set to Cool and the set temperature is below room temperature, check that the air filter isn't clogged, and confirm supply and return vents aren't blocked. Check the breaker for the outdoor unit too. If it still isn't cooling, turn the system off so a frozen coil or failing part doesn't get worse, then call us at (512) 960-5282.

faq.q: Should I repair or replace my air conditioner?
faq.a: Repair usually makes sense when the system is fairly young and the problem is a single part. Replacement is worth pricing out when the unit is around 15 years old, your energy bills keep climbing, it needs repairs several times a year, or one repair approaches the cost of a new system. We'll tell you honestly which side of that line you're on. Many of our reviews mention we didn't push a replacement that wasn't needed.

faq.q: Do you offer emergency HVAC service?
faq.a: Yes. Emergency heating and air conditioning service is available 24/7. Call (512) 960-5282, day or night.
We're based at 342 Jefferson Dr in Kyle and serve Kyle, Buda, Austin, San Marcos, Wimberley, Woodcreek, Dripping Springs, Driftwood, Mountain City and Hays.

faq.q: Which brands do you work on?
faq.a: All major brands and models, including Carrier, Bryant, Lennox, Goodman, American Standard and York. Our recent installs include Bryant, Carrier and Goodman systems.

faq.q: How often should my AC and heater be serviced?
faq.a: At least once a year for each. Ideally that means an AC tune-up in spring before the Central Texas heat and a heating check in fall before the first cold front. Our Gold Service Plan covers both visits.

faq.q: Do you offer financing on a new system?
faq.a: Yes. Financing is available through FTL Finance, and you can apply online. Ask us about it when we quote your new system.

faq.q: Can you help with allergies or dusty air in my home?
faq.a: Yes. We install whole-home air quality products such as upgraded filtration and air purifiers that capture dust, pollen, pet dander and mold spores. We'll look at your system and recommend what fits your home.
Yes. Climate Control Solutions holds Texas air conditioning contractor license TACLB77818E, and our team is licensed, insured and trained.

faq.a: Call (512) 960-5282 or use the Book online button to pick a time. If you'd rather talk first, call and we'll answer your questions before you schedule.

services.lede: When your air conditioner quits in a Central Texas summer, you need someone who shows up on time, finds the real problem and fixes it without upselling you. That's how we've built 662 Google reviews.
signs: It's blowing warm or weak air
A failing capacitor, low refrigerant, a dirty coil or a blocked filter can all cut cooling. We test each part instead of guessing.
Grinding, banging or screeching
A low steady hum is normal. Metal-on-metal sounds usually mean a motor, fan or compressor problem that gets more expensive if it keeps running.
Burning or musty smells
A burning smell can mean overheating electrical parts. Shut the system off and call. A musty smell often points to moisture or mold in the system.
Short-cycling
If the system turns on and off before finishing a cycle, it wastes power and wears out parts. Causes range from thermostat issues to an oversized or overheating unit.
The house feels sticky
Your AC removes humidity as well as heat. A muggy house with the AC running is a sign something isn't working right.
Water around the indoor unit
A clogged condensate drain or frozen coil can leak into ceilings and closets. Catching it early prevents water damage.
services.body_title: How an AC repair visit works
body: We diagnose the whole system, not just the symptom. We check electrical parts, refrigerant levels, airflow, coils and drains so the same problem doesn't come back next week.

You'll get a clear explanation of what's wrong and your options before any work starts. If a repair is the smart call, we'll do the repair. If your system is near the end of its life, we'll tell you straight and help you compare.
We repair every major brand and model, and we keep the visit as quick and quiet as possible so you can get back to your day.

services.lede: Texas cold snaps don't last long, but they hit hard. When your furnace or heat pump stops keeping up, we'll diagnose it fast and get your home warm again.
signs: Cold or lukewarm air
A bad igniter, a heat pump stuck in the wrong mode or a failing part can all keep your system from heating.
It won't turn on or keeps shutting off
Safety switches, thermostats, flame sensors and wiring problems can cause no-starts and short-cycling.
Unusual noises or smells
Banging, squealing or a burning smell that lasts beyond the first run of the season should be checked.
Higher bills with less comfort
A system that runs constantly but can't keep up is wasting energy and wearing itself out.
body: We test the whole heating system, including ignition, burners, safety controls, airflow and the thermostat, so we fix the cause and not just the symptom.
For gas furnaces, we check for safe operation, including a carbon monoxide safety test. For heat pumps, we check refrigerant, the reversing valve and defrost controls.
Emergency service is available 24/7. If your heat goes out on a cold night, call (512) 960-5282.
